Resolves #21849

The label sentence that leads the README's second part, the portal's head and the `llms.txt` header now pitches what the peers do: *Neo.mjs is an agent institution: AI peers from rival labs who own their work, hold each other to account, and improve their own tools and rules.* The README's first-screen sentence and its deployment pitch follow it. Memory and the public record stay in the text as means. ADR 0018 §2.3 carries the new sentence with its amendment line. No number, no door and no hero text changes.

Evidence: L3 (GitHub's render of the pushed head, logged out, at 1440 × 900 and 390 × 844; `seo.json` compared per route with its generator's output) → L3 required (AC-5 and AC-6 judge the rendered page). No residuals.

Change class: zero-delta (`docs`). agent-preflight: not hosted here; `check-relative-links` ran on the head.
Prescription checked: `apps/portal/index.html` and `buildScripts/docs/seo/generate.mjs` — own the head and the `llms.txt` header; `seo.json` derives from `index.html` through `seoJson.mjs`. The label is still typed on five hand-edited surfaces and one test pin. A coherence check across them (ADR 0018 §2.4, mechanism 3) would own "one sentence" better; it is not built here.
Substrate: ADR 0018 is not turn-loaded; its Amended row is the lifecycle record. Decision Record impact: amends §2.3.

## The wording, and why

The hero stopped pitching the team by its means on 20 Nov (`#21595`), and ADR 0018 §2.3 says so: "Continuity, memory and the public record are means, not the pitch." The label two entries above still did.

| Place | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| The label: `README.md:105`, the portal's head, `llms.txt`, ADR 0018 §2.3 | persistent AI maintainers with identities, memory, peer review, and a record anyone can read | AI peers from rival labs who own their work, hold each other to account, and improve their own tools and rules |
| `README.md:21`, the first screen | named AI maintainers from rival labs (Claude, Gemini, GPT) with memory and cross-family peer review, and one human at the merge gate | AI peers from rival labs (Claude, Gemini, GPT) who own their work, review and reject each other's pull requests, and improve their own tools and rules, with one human at the merge gate |
| `README.md:186`, the deployment pitch | a swarm like the one that maintains Neo, with a persistent Memory Core, cross-family review, and DreamService self-improvement; a standing engineering institution with memory and peer review | you get the conditions, not our team: agents of your own that learn your code, own their work on it, review and reject each other's pull requests, and improve their own tools and rules; the Knowledge Base and the Memory Core are the means |

Each new claim has its receipt on the page or one link away. "Own their work" and "review and reject" stand in the record block under the first screen (1,125 approved across model families, 463 sent back for changes). "Improve their own tools and rules" is the merged history of `neomjs/neo-agent-skills`. "The conditions, not our team" is `learn/benefits/Introduction.md`, sections 4 and 8.

## Deltas from ticket

- **AC-6's second clause binds the CTO only.** It first asked both visitors to name ownership or accountability across labs. The engineer names the worker architecture, which is the right answer for his link. The ticket's body says when and why it was reworded.
- **`seo.json` carries the generator's output for three routes:** `/`, `/home` and the ADR's own page. A full regeneration changes 14 more routes that already differ on `dev` (out of scope, noted in defect-note `c9a3525179d47d47`); `buildScripts/release/prepare.mjs` regenerates the file at the cut.
- **The portal's head says "rival labs" in a machine-read description.** The Introduction's search description already does. The reviewer of the crawler half may still want the colder form there.

Kept: the line it costs is the one the blind read asked for (`## Cold look`). (2) At 390 the link breaks across two lines: kept, it is the sentence's proof. (3) The deployment paragraph is six dense lines before and after: its length is not changed here. (4) "v13 turns it outward" stands above it on the day Engine 14 ships: a fact line, outside this ticket. (5) The npm badge reads v13.4.0 until the publish: resolves itself.

Outside CI, on the head: `npm run check-relative-links` (441 links resolved).

## Cold look

One reader without session context per round (Explore, Sonnet), frames unlabelled and named P and Q, the released first screen as a blind control, desktop and phone. Two visitors with ten seconds each: **E**, a senior web engineer who followed "Neo.mjs 14 is out: a multi-threaded JavaScript application engine with grids, Gantt, scheduler and boards"; **C**, a CTO who followed "a team of AI agents from different labs that maintains a real codebase in public". The grade is "I know what I get and what to do next", 1 to 10.

| Round | Changed head | Released | Changed | The reader's reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `2f65430e80`, without the merge-gate clause | E 6 · C 7 | E 6 · C 6 | "one human at the merge gate" answers the CTO's accountability question inside the sentence; on the phone the record's "every merge by one human" is cut off |
| 2 | `cefa81b741`, the clause restored | E 6 · C 6 | E 6 · C 7 | "review and reject each other's pull requests" says what the agents do and is itself the link; "named", "with memory" and "cross-family peer review" are labels left undefined |

- **The engineer sees no difference in either round.** What he acts on is the engine paragraph and the "Build with it" line, identical in both.
- **The control moved by one between the rounds** (C 7, then 6), so a one-point gap is inside one reader's noise. The reasons are the stable part, and they point the same way: the human belongs in the sentence, and a verb reads better than a label.
- **"What does this have that nothing else I know has?"** The CTO on the changed screen: "Agents from rival labs rejecting each other's PRs and improving their own rules, with a month of public counts; I know single-vendor bots." The engineer: logic in workers across a whole widget set, "unproven on this screen".
- **The gap to 9, and its fate.** The engineer: no benchmark or code on the first screen, the npm badge still reads v13.4.0, and on the phone the install line and the cover sit below the first screen. The CTO: "who audits the rule changes?", and "Agent OS" is undefined on this screen. All of it is the first screen's composition, settled in `#21564`, not this change's words: not changed here.
